scene_name: Accepted backlog under healthy cash and sufficient material, but one small line is too small at handoff

what_the_company_already_has: one fully staffed main market that is activated early in prewarm
one small production line that becomes available early in prewarm
one external supplier that can replenish later if needed
one completed pilot order proving the business is already operating
enough raw material to cover the committed backlog
what_the_company_lacks: enough effective line capacity to digest the committed delivery rhythm

day0_to_day1.goal: Establish a live business baseline by activating one fully staffed main market first and then activating the first real production cycle once the small line becomes available.
must_show: one fully staffed main market exists before the first order appears
one pilot order exists and then becomes accepted
the company is not a cold startup anymore
the small line moves from construction to availability

day2_to_day5.goal: Accumulate future-dated accepted backlog while keeping production real and raw material clearly safe.
must_show: accepted backlog grows across several days
finished goods rise through real production

day6_to_day9.goal: Freeze the bottleneck instead of repairing it before takeover.
must_show: accepted backlog remains future-dated rather than already breached
no purchase order has been placed yet
one fully staffed main market remains active but is not the lead problem
the only small line remains occupied or fully committed at handoff

handoff_success_story: Production should read the snapshot as an expansion problem.
Procurement should not ask for immediate replenishment first because material still is sufficient.
Sales should not be the first responder because committed demand is already present.
Inventory should confirm that line throughput is the gating resource rather than warehouse pressure.
